overall: At 01:35 ET, Atlanta is sitting at 73.4°F with zero upward velocity, indicating early morning conditions with temperatures yet to begin their daytime climb. The dewpoint of 64.4°F signals notable humidity that could limit or modulate afternoon heating, and a modest 8.1 mph wind adds some mixing. Given the time of day, this is essentially the overnight floor — the full warming window from solar heating still lies ahead.
forecast_obs_notes: There is meaningful model spread today: HRRR is the outlier low at 75.5°F, while ECMWF (78.7°F) and NBM (79.2°F) cluster roughly 3-4°F higher, suggesting HRRR may be capturing a more aggressive cloud or moisture scenario. The ensemble signals complicate the picture further — the odd model flags 81-82°F as its top bin at 29% with Tier 1 confidence, while the even model shows 80-81°F at only 20% (Tier 4, Avoid), indicating divergence between ensemble frameworks on tail upside risk.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence favors a daily high in the upper 78-79°F range, anchored by the ECMWF/NBM consensus and discounting the lower HRRR somewhat. The high-humidity dewpoint (64.4°F) and current flat velocity suggest limited early momentum, but Atlanta in mid-June retains strong solar forcing that can push temps well past the overnight reading; HRRR's 75.5°F ceiling appears too conservative given the NBM/ECMWF alignment. Confidence is moderate — the Tier 1 odd-model signal for 81-82°F introduces non-trivial upside risk, but without stronger model agreement or observed acceleration, 79°F is the best central estimate.
